messages:
eval-bot: nightly-eval complete for `rwd-v3-small` variants on `nightly/multilang/loc_mix_v2`. Summary: KOR->EN BLEU delta -6.2 (int8-fused vs fp16), COMET -0.35, AR->EN politeness-regression +12% failure rate. Top artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/1769502468/report.html

Julia Tran: ugh, saw that alert — thanks for the ping. seems correlated with the int8-fused rollout that hit canary last night. tagging @Vikram @Mai

Vikram Singh: on it. my first suspicion is the fused softmax/scale kernel change landed in the quant branch. can we bisect between commits that touched fused-kernels? which commit range does the nightly runner use?

Julia Tran: CI run metadata -> commit range abc123..def456. I kicked off a bisect job (runner erg-342) across that range; link: https://ci.redwood/runs/erg-342. job artifacts will land at s3://redwood-evals/bisect/erg-342/

Mai Nguyen: I pulled a couple failing examples. For KOR->EN example id=KOR_1872: source: "선생님께서 말씀하신대로 했습니다."
fp16 output: "I did as the teacher asked."
int8-fused output: "I did as the teacher."  <-- lost honorific phrasing, feels less polite.

Chris Patel: reproducer command I'm running locally:
```
./evaluate \
  --model rwd-v3-small \
  --variant int8-fused \
  --subset kor_ar_samples \
  --metrics bleu,comet,chrF \
  --seed 42 \
  --max_len 256
```
Posting results back when done.

Vikram Singh: early bisect hit at commit def789 where `fused_softmax_v2` was introduced (file: kernels/softmax_fused.cu). reverting that commit locally flipped the KOR example back to fp16-like output in a quick smoke test. pushing a test branch now.

eval-bot: note: tokenization/detok parity check shows chrF drop aligns with BLEU drop for the KOR subset. Tokenization pipeline reported identical token counts between variants, but detokenized punctuation differed in ~8% of KOR cases.

Mai Nguyen: interesting — for AR examples I've seen politeness markers (e.g., "حضرتك") replaced by neutral pronouns. I suspect postprocessing detokenizer or a script that normalizes diacritics. running a tokenization-only diff now: `python tools/tokenize_compare.py --a=fp16 --b=int8 --lang=ar --ids 102,117,233`

Chris Patel: tokenization diff for KOR shows the int8 path lowercases some terminal particles in our detok step: diff output attached (short):
```
- ...했습니다.
+ ...했습니다
```
missing final period in detok in several outputs. Could be a stray strip in `postproc/cleanup.py` changed by fused-kernel build or packaging.

Vikram Singh: also noted the canary machines where the int8-fused build ran last night had CUDA 12.2, while our fp16 baseline used 12.1 in the hosted fleet. kernel numerics + driver ABI sometimes shift rounding behavior. adding driver version to the bisect matrix.

Julia Tran: plan: 1) finish bisect to isolate commit (Vikram) 2) reproduce locally with the exact driver and packaging (Chris) 3) run tokenization-only regression to rule out detok (Mai) 4) if kernel bug, revert fused change or add a guard for locale-sensitive ops. I'll drive coordination.

Vikram Singh: created branch `revert/fused-softmax-def789` and ran quick smoke -> KOR/AR examples look nominal vs fp16. pushing test build to canary-1 for the eval job.

Mai Nguyen: uploading minimal repro snippets and tokenization diffs to s3://redwood-evals/bisect/erg-342/repro/ (files: kor_1872.{src,fp16.txt,int8.txt}, ar_102.{src,fp16.txt,int8.txt})

Chris Patel: eval harness queued on canary-1 with the revert build. job id: ehr-9002. expected finish ~2h. I'll post metrics and top failure samples when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Vikram Singh: if ehr-9002 passes with BLEU/COMET restored, we'll merge hotfix and schedule a redeploy to nightly. driver matrix tests ongoing. :thumbsup:

Julia Tran: great. assigning owners: Vikram (kernel bisect & PR), Mai (tokenization diffs & repro), Chris (harness runs & canary verification). I will update the incident board and ping infra for driver parity check. keeping thread open. :eyes:

Mai Nguyen: ack, will follow up with a small patch suggestion for detok cleanup if needed.

Chris Patel: noted. will post results in this thread.

Julia Tran: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage.
